title: Derived internal Hom at finite coefficients
statement: Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $\dim X\leq m$ for $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, using topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Work on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with constant coefficient sheaf $A_X$. Write $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ for bounded constructible complexes [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] of finite Tor amplitude: the etale version of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], meaning that tensoring with any $A_X$-module sheaf in degree zero has cohomology only in some fixed finite interval. Let $K,M$ be in this category, with Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$, respectively, for integers $a\leq b$ and $c\leq d$. Then the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and has Tor amplitude in $[c-b-2m,d-a+2m]$. If $K$ is site-perfect, meaning that locally on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ it is isomorphic to a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], the sharper interval $[c-b,d-a]$ holds.

proof.text: The characteristic of the finite base field is p, by its cardinality p^a, and the algebraic closure has the same characteristic. The coefficient absolute value satisfies |ell|<1. The DVR description puts ell in the maximal ideal generated by the chosen uniformizer; raising to n shows ell^n=0 in A_{E,n}. Since ell differs from p, ell^n is a unit in the base field and in the global sections of its spectrum. This supplies HasInvertibleExponent for the lifted coefficient ring, and its pullback to X.

proof.text: Apply the existing, proved source declarations Etale.boundedConstructible_derivedHom and Etale.torAmplitudeIn_derivedHom to the lifted finite coefficient ring and X over the algebraically closed field. Their proofs are exactly the general branch of this unit: a finite affine cover reduces to separated finite-type charts with dimension at most m, and the source declaration constructibleFiniteTor_derivedHom_of_isSeparated implements cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom by Verdier biduality and the two dual Tor bounds. The adopted open-cover lemmas descend bounded constructibility and the uniform interval [c-b-2m,d-a+2m], including the empty-cover case. Thus reuse those implementations instead of reconstructing ringed-site and coefficient-category comparisons.

proof.text: For the sharper clause use the proved source implication IsSitePerfect.isDualizable, which proves dualizability by finite-free retracts on the perfectness cover and conservativity. Apply Etale.torAmplitudeIn_derivedHom_of_isDualizable_aux: the coefficient dual has Tor interval [-b,-a], and RHom(K,M) is its derived tensor product with M, so its interval is [c-b,d-a]. This is the dualizable case explicitly permitted by the current unit proof and requires no geometric Verdier duality.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q32-c393e077b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item statement (unchanged and not weakened; étale site with constant A_X coefficients, same as cor-weil-finite-constructible-hom; no base-change morphism involved), every step, the three new nodes, the statements of all cited nodes, the master blueprint source (order 2199), and the unit. The main-20261015 snapshot does not restate this unit. No SGA source is cited. Steps 1-5 and 7-10 are correct as delivered. I checked the [c-b,d-a] endpoint arithmetic and the Hom-complex differential and sign. The unit's example (closed point of A^1, m=1) is consistent with the bounds. I found and repaired three faults. (1) C5 duplicate: lem-sf-open-immersion-derived-degree-zero, H^0(Rj_*B)=j_*B, is the case v=j_* of the Mathlib leaf lem-sp-derived-well-defined (R^0v=v, with R^q u_* = H^q(Ru_*) by def-weil-pbc-direct-image). I dropped it. (2) B4: lem-sf-cech-kernel-open-cover stores \bigoplus as the JSON escape \b (backspace) followed by 'igoplus', and its index order i<j is never introduced. The whole Čech/open-direct-image detour (old Steps 6-8, using thm-fin-open-immersion and thm-constructible-serre) is unnecessary anyway. lem-weil-pbc-constructible-qcqs-affine-local, already cited in Step 3, gives (3)⇒(1) on the affine U_i and (2)⇒(3) on the qcqs X directly. I replaced old Steps 6-8 with one step citing it and dropped the node. (3) C4/E1 in old Step 12 (now Step 10): it referred to 'the site cover in Step 6' and 'Step 8', which are stale numbers (the cover is in old Step 9, the window in old Step 11). It also reused the Step 5 argument, but the cover-vanishing lemma there covered only finite open covers, while the site-perfect cover is an arbitrary étale covering. I generalized lem-sf-sheaf-zero-on-open-cover to any covering family of X_et; this is true by the separatedness of the sheaf on the pulled-back covering, and I checked the empty, one-member and zero cases. Step 10 now cites it with the correct step references and the restriction lemmas. I searched the DAG for duplicates of the kept node and found none; the nearest are stage3-categorical-finite-cover-local-zero and lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-zero-neighbourhood, which state different things. Corrected files: fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/thm-sf-hom-ctf.json (10 steps; proof_deps is the union of the step uses; split_report.tool_uses no longer lists lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type or thm-constructible-serre) and fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-sf-sheaf-zero-on-open-cover.json.
